articles.title: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss
articles.summary: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss
articles.summaryTr: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
articles.articleText: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss - Published Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia, in his first public comments since his shock resignation. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. But he said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia. As the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company. The prospect of Huang returning at this point looks unlikely. The company's board is investigating his conduct, which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive. The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang. Beyond the internal Nvidia investigation, Huang's affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Beijing is set to see the billionaire questioned before multiple committees of US lawmakers in the weeks ahead. The Nvidia founder said he had "made serious mistakes in my personal life". Nonetheless, Huang's statement appeared to show some hope he would be able to move past the major corporate scandal. Huang said people have continued to "reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics". "If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang added. Many technology executives in recent days have praised Huang's role in the artificial intelligence boom. A petition began circulating online over the weekend calling for his reinstatement at the company. Yet, by Monday, many executives were not openly calling for Huang's return. Brad Gerstner, a major tech investor who knows Huang personally and also holds a significant stake in Nvidia, last week wrote an open letter saying that Nvidia could consider Huang's reinstatement. On Monday, Gerstner said during an event hosted by Semafor that his letter had been misunderstood and the investigation into Huang's conduct needed to run its course. While Gerstner questioned the facts around Huang's departure, he added: "I don't know to what degree he misled the board. If I was on a board I would take that very seriously. Let's be clear no one is above the law."

articles.title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
articles.summary: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
articles.summaryTr: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
articles.articleText: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements - Published The UK has sanctioned companies it said are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory. The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank. The construction of settlements, which are illegal under international law, has risen sharply in recent years. There has also been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property. Israel is yet to comment on the announcement, but has previously condemned UK sanctions related to West Bank settlements, accusing the Labour government of "systematically acting against the State of Israel". The Palestinian foreign ministry welcomed the sanctions and called on other countries to follow suit. It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the highly sensitive E1 area east of Jerusalem. The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and cut it off from East Jerusalem. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine". The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza. Responding to the announcement, the group said: "Tzav 9 is a movement of abiding citizens from all the political spectrum, and we've always protested peacefully." It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world. The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements and the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK. Miliband said: "Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach. "That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution. "The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable. "We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike." 'New approach' In September, the UK government announced that it would ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements, as well as acting against companies and individuals providing services for settlement expansion. At the time, Miliband said the move marked the beginning of a "new approach" to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which "not only calls out injustice and suffering, but acts". That announcement prompted a furious reaction from Israel, which said it would shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem in retaliation. Last month, most diplomats left the consulate - which handled UK relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem as well as in the West Bank and Gaza - but the UK insisted that the building would not be closing and would operate as a "UK mission". Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them. There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. - Israel opens up bids for highly sensitive West Bank settlement project - Published20 August Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

articles.title: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
articles.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
articles.summaryTr: Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.
articles.articleText: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains. US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller cited the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack while raising questions about security and accountability in tokenized financial markets, suggesting that major institutional transactions may require blockchain systems offering greater privacy and control. Speaking at The Clearing House’s annual conference in New York on Nov. 17, an event bringing together banking and payments industry leaders, Waller questioned who would bear responsibility when fraudsters exploit smart contracts, private keys are compromised, transfers go wrong or assets become stranded on failed blockchains. Waller said the level of security and oversight required could depend on the importance of the financial transactions involved: For example, systemically important financial transactions may call for the most conservative designs. These designs might trade some of the developer creativity found on purely permissionless, open networks in favor of greater privacy and control. The expansion of tokenized finance would also require clear legal frameworks governing ownership rights, custody and settlement, he said, arguing that governance and legal protections are as important as technical safeguards in building trust. Waller’s remarks came as four Democratic senators pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over safeguards for tokenized stocks. In a letter released Monday, the lawmakers questioned who would be responsible for shares transferred outside regulated platforms and whether regulators could freeze or recover the tokens. Related: Custodia Bank loses Supreme Court bid for direct Fed payment access Barr warns of AI-related cybersecurity risks Waller wasn’t the only Federal Reserve governor to raise concerns about emerging financial technologies this week. His remarks followed a Monday speech by fellow Fed Governor Michael Barr, who warned that artificial intelligence could introduce new cybersecurity risks as financial institutions increasingly adopt the technology. Barr said AI-enabled attackers were exploiting vulnerabilities previously considered too difficult to target, while autonomous AI systems could behave in ways that undermine security controls “Attackers only need to be right once, while defenders need to be right all the time,” Barr said. He also said major banks had reported finding AI agents attempting to take actions in retail customer accounts without being able to verify their authenticity or authorization, highlighting the need for stronger authentication and security controls. articles.title: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
articles.summary: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
articles.summaryTr: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".
articles.articleText: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington - Published President Donald Trump has said the US is taking "very seriously" the potential for any Iranian plot to attack Washington DC, after he was asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments. In the Philippines, where he attended the Asean Summit, Trump nodded when asked by a journalist about the report that Tehran was planning to detonate a so-called dirty bomb in the US capital and said: "We're looking into it." CNN cited unnamed US intelligence officials suggesting Iran could target senior figures in Trump's administration with such an attack. Iran called the claim "baseless." Concerns about dirty bombs grew after the 9/11 attacks in 2001, although no such attack has ever occurred. Such a device would contain radioactive material - such as uranium - which would be scattered through the air when its conventional explosive detonated. The BBC has not independently verified CNN's reporting. During his comments to reporters in Manila, Trump was asked whether there was reason to believe an attack was imminent. "I hope it's not," he said, "but we take it very seriously because they [the Iranians] happen to be crazy." In a statement before Trump's comments, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis wrote: "We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland." Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rebutted the CNN article and other US reports. He posted on X: "Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations." Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's parliamentary speaker and chief negotiator in indirect talks with the US, responded to the report saying it was part of a "messaging operation". "Same false flags, same war mongering, new logos," he wrote on X. Mick Mulroy, a former CIA paramilitary officer and deputy assistant defence secretary, told the BBC: "A dirty bomb is not difficult to make or deploy." "Although it is not a weapon of mass destruction, it can be a weapon of mass disruption," he added. Imran Bayoumi, a geostrategy expert with the Atlantic Council in Washington DC and former policy adviser to the defence department, said that it remains "unclear how serious" would be the threat of a supposed Iranian dirty bomb. "But Iran has planned and threatened to attack the US in the past," he said. "It is also unclear why this report is becoming public now." It comes as intelligence officials and members of the Trump administration seek congressional renewal of a key national security law. Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (Fisa), which allows the US to spy on foreign nationals, expires next March.

articles.title: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
articles.summary: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
articles.summaryTr: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
articles.articleText: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge - Published The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions. Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted. Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around. At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide. The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours. Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet. Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles. Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions. "It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection. But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful. "It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that." From the damage, it looks like Russia targeted the same spot on the bridge with a volley of three missiles, aiming to keep the road closed for as long as possible. A major recovery operation is under way, with firefighters and engineers in fluorescent overalls working to evaluate the extent of the damage. But it looks like the disruption will continue for some time. Further along the Dnipro River, the Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was also hit on Monday night, with four missiles. The metro line across it was suspended for a while, although by mid-afternoon it had been restored. The mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said road transport in one direction was also being partially restored. On the Pivnichnyi bridge, a man with a bag of tennis rackets on his back was gazing at the crater in front of him. He was heading home from the courts after he had travelled on foot to the left bank. "It is upsetting," Anatolii told us. "Then when you read the news of what our side did to the Crimea bridge, you do feel a bit better." That is because there was a battle of the bridges overnight. Ukrainian missiles hit the one Russia had built to occupied Crimea, and caused serious damage. That bridge is prized by Russian President Vladimir Putin personally, a symbol of his illegal 2014 takeover. Ukrainians loathe it for the same reason and now a section has collapsed into the sea, along with its towering arch. To many here, the timing feels significant: a blow to Putin's image, just as he wants to seem most powerful at this week's summit with the US and China. But for Kyiv resident Antonina, today is just another challenge to overcome. The 67-year-old, who we met pulling a shopping trolley through the debris on a bridge in the Ukrainian capital, was heading to see her son on the right bank, but taxi drivers were charging a fortune to go round, so she decided to walk. "What else could I do?" she shrugged. "It was a very scary night. It felt like something exploded right over my head. We will get through this, but I just wish the war would end." - Published52 minutes ago

articles.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
articles.summary: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
articles.summaryTr: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
articles.articleText: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers - Published After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections. The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness. PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year. "These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination." He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission. Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates. US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years. Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections. Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status". "Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans. "Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities." The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards". The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths. But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems. The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns. An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials. Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database. Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics. The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge. President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine. Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates. "It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top." The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices. - Published24 July - Published30 January - Published24 September

articles.articleText: Borsa İstanbul düşerken 7 hisse tavan yaptı! İşte günün yıldızları ve kaybettirenleri BIST 100 endeksi günü yüzde 1,53 düşüşle 11.661 puandan tamamlarken bazı hisseler yüzde 10'a yakın yükseldi. İşte 17 Kasım 2026'da borsada en çok kazandıran ve kaybettiren hisseler… Borsa düşerken hangi hisseler yükseldi? articles.titleTr: Adalet Bakanı Gürlek açıkladı: Fon soruşturmasında 40,4 milyar TL geri alındı
articles.summaryTr: Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, fon soruşturmalarında 75 kişiden yaklaşık 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildiğini açıkladı. Soruşturma kapsamında 129 şüpheli tutuklu, 289 şüpheli ise adli kontrol altında bulunuyor.
articles.articleText: Adalet Bakanı Gürlek açıkladı: Fon soruşturmasında 40,4 milyar TL geri alındı - Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, fon soruşturmalarında 75 kişiden yaklaşık 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildiğini açıkladı. Soruşturma kapsamında 129 şüpheli tutuklu, 289 şüpheli ise adli kontrol altında bulunuyor. Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturmalarında gelinen son durumu açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturmaların yeni deliller doğrultusunda genişletildiğini belirten Gürlek, bugüne kadar 498 şüphelinin soruşturma kapsamına alındığını bildirdi. Gürlek'in paylaştığı bilgilere göre 129 şüpheli tutuklu, 289 şüpheli hakkında ise adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanıyor. Hakkında yakalama kararı bulunan 54 şüpheliye yönelik çalışmalar sürerken, gözaltındaki 22 şüphelinin adli işlemleri devam ediyor. 75 kişiden 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildi Soruşturmalar kapsamında gönüllü iade ve geri kazanım çalışmaları sonucunda 75 kişiden yaklaşık 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildi. Gürlek, gönüllü iadenin hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmayacağını vurgulayarak, “Gönüllü iade yapılması, tek başına hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmaz” ifadelerini kullandı. 417 kişi ve 149 şirketin malvarlığına tedbir Suçtan elde edildiği değerlendirilen gelirlerin kaçırılmasını önlemek amacıyla 417 gerçek kişi ve 149 tüzel kişinin malvarlıkları hakkında el koyma ve dondurma kararı uygulandığını açıklayan Gürlek, para hareketleri, malvarlığı devirleri ve bağlantılı hesapların ayrıntılı incelendiğini belirtti. Denetim süreçlerine ilişkin iddialar da inceleniyor Gürlek, fon yöneticileri ve piyasa aktörlerinin yanı sıra denetim süreçlerine ilişkin iddiaların da soruşturma kapsamında değerlendirildiğini bildirdi. Kamu görevlileri dahil hukuki sorumluluk doğurabilecek tüm hususların yetkili adli makamlarca incelendiğini belirten Gürlek, hiçbir iddianın peşinen doğru kabul edilmeyeceğini ve somut delillerin göz ardı edilmeyeceğini ifade etti. Fon Koordinasyon Kurulu'nun 10'uncu toplantısı yapıldı Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz başkanlığında, ilgili kurumların temsilcilerinin katılımıyla 10'uncu Fon Koordinasyon Kurulu Toplantısı gerçekleştirildi. Toplantıda soruşturmaların seyri, mali incelemeler, uygulanan tedbirler ve yatırımcıların haklarının korunmasına yönelik çalışmalar değerlendirildi.

articles.title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.summaryTr: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
articles.articleText: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine - Published Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort. The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - had been closed after Russia hit Ukraine's capital overnight. The Southern bridge partially reopened on Tuesday, Klitschko said. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good. While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin. The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight. The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014. The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018. In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands. "We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC. He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians". Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got." The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage". The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies. On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge. Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage". The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies. On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge. Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. articles.titleTr: Tümosan'da (TMSN) kar tablosu tersine döndü: İşte şirketin 3. çeyrek bilançosu
articles.summaryTr: Tümosan, 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında 2,88 milyar TL net zarar açıkladı. Geçen yılın aynı döneminde 9,17 milyar TL kâr eden şirketin satış gelirleri yıllık bazda yüzde 1 geriledi.
articles.articleText: Tümosan'da (TMSN) kar tablosu tersine döndü: İşte şirketin 3. çeyrek bilançosu - Tümosan, 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında 2,88 milyar TL net zarar açıkladı. Geçen yılın aynı döneminde 9,17 milyar TL kâr eden şirketin satış gelirleri yıllık bazda yüzde 1 geriledi. Tümosan Motor ve Traktör Sanayi A.Ş. (TMSN), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde 2 milyar 882 milyon 522 bin TL net zarar açıkladı. Tümosan, geçen yılın aynı döneminde 9 milyar 176 milyon 590 bin TL net kâr elde etmişti. Şirketin yalnızca üçüncü çeyrekteki net zararı ise 486 milyon 956 bin TL oldu. Satış gelirleri yüzde 1 geriledi Tümosan'ın 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında elde ettiği hasılat, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yaklaşık yüzde 1 azalarak 3 milyar 139,8 milyon TL'ye geriledi. Şirketin temel faaliyet göstergelerinde ise geçen yılın aynı dönemine kıyasla iyileşme görüldü. - Esas faaliyet zararı: 1,80 milyar TL'den 759,1 milyon TL'ye geriledi. - FAVÖK zararı: 1,12 milyar TL'den 630,5 milyon TL'ye geriledi. Borçlar yükseldi, özkaynaklar geriledi Tümosan'ın 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla toplam varlıkları 29,94 milyar TL olarak kaydedildi. Şirketin toplam borçları 2025 yıl sonundaki 11,98 milyar TL seviyesinden 14,40 milyar TL'ye yükseldi. Özkaynakları ise aynı dönemde 18,42 milyar TL'den 15,54 milyar TL'ye geriledi. TMSN hisselerinde piyasa değeri 5,9 milyar TL Paylaşılan şirket çarpanlarına göre Tümosan'ın piyasa değeri 5,90 milyar TL, piyasa değeri/defter değeri (PD/DD) oranı ise 0,38 olarak açıklandı. Şirketin fiyat/kazanç (F/K) oranı ise tabloda hesaplanmamış durumda.

articles.titleTr: Jensen Huang'dan CEO'luk koltuğuna dönüş mesajı: “Hatalarımın sorumluluğunu alıyorum”
articles.summaryTr: Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang, yönetim kurulunun şirketin, hissedarların ve çalışanların çıkarları doğrultusunda karar vermesi halinde görevine dönmekten onur duyacağını söyledi. Huang, yönetim kurulunun bağımsız soruşturmasıyla iş birliği yapacağını da açıkladı.
articles.articleText: Jensen Huang'dan CEO'luk koltuğuna dönüş mesajı: “Hatalarımın sorumluluğunu alıyorum” - Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang, yönetim kurulunun şirketin, hissedarların ve çalışanların çıkarları doğrultusunda karar vermesi halinde görevine dönmekten onur duyacağını söyledi. Huang, yönetim kurulunun bağımsız soruşturmasıyla iş birliği yapacağını da açıkladı. Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang, görevine geri dönme ihtimaline ilişkin dikkat çeken açıklamalarda bulundu. Wall Street Journal'a yaptığı değerlendirmede Huang, yönetim kurulunun kendisinin CEO olarak dönmesinin hissedarlar, çalışanlar, şirket ve ABD'nin çıkarlarına uygun olduğuna karar vermesi halinde bu görevi yeniden üstlenmekten onur duyacağını belirtti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Huang, yönetim kuruluna sorun yarattığını kabul ederek, “Derin pişmanlık duyduğum sorunlara yol açtım. Hatalarımın sorumluluğunu tamamen alıyorum” ifadelerini kullandı. Bağımsız soruşturmayla iş birliği yapacak Huang, yönetim kurulunun yürüttüğü bağımsız soruşturmayla iş birliği yapmaya kararlı olduğunu da vurguladı. Görevinden ayrılmasının ardından çalışanlardan, yatırımcılardan, iş ortaklarından ve müşterilerden CEO olarak geri dönmesi yönünde yoğun çağrılar aldığını öne süren Huang, nihai kararın yönetim kuruluna ait olduğunun altını çizdi.

Şirketin tasarruf ve dönüşüm programı kapsamında 4 bin 600'e kadar çalışanla yolların ayrılması beklenirken, bazı görevlerin yapay zeka ve teknolojiyle yürütülmesi hedefleniyor.

articles.summaryTr: İngiliz tütün şirketi Imperial Brands, 2030 sonuna kadar küresel iş gücünün yüzde 16 ila 18'ini azaltmayı planlıyor. Şirketin tasarruf ve dönüşüm programı kapsamında 4 bin 600'e kadar çalışanla yolların ayrılması beklenirken, bazı görevlerin yapay zeka ve teknolojiyle yürütülmesi hedefleniyor.
articles.articleText: Tütün devinden 4 bin 600 kişilik işten çıkarma planı: Yapay zeka da devrede - İngiliz tütün şirketi Imperial Brands, 2030 sonuna kadar küresel iş gücünün yüzde 16 ila 18'ini azaltmayı planlıyor. - Şirketin tasarruf ve dönüşüm programı kapsamında 4 bin 600'e kadar çalışanla yolların ayrılması beklenirken, bazı görevlerin yapay zeka ve teknolojiyle yürütülmesi hedefleniyor. İngiltere merkezli tütün şirketi Imperial Brands, maliyetleri düşürmek ve operasyonlarını yeniden yapılandırmak amacıyla kapsamlı bir işten çıkarma programı başlatıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 2030 yılı sonuna kadar toplam 4 bin 600 kişiyi işten çıkarmayı planlıyor. Şirketin açıklamasına göre, eylül ayında sona eren 2026 mali yılı kapsamında 2 bin 100 pozisyonun azaltılması süreci devam ediyor. 2030 sonuna kadar ise 2 bin 100 ila 2 bin 500 kişinin daha işten çıkarılması bekleniyor. İngiltere, ABD, Avrupa ve Avustralya'daki operasyonlarında toplam 25 bin 800 kişi çalıştıran şirketin planı, küresel iş gücünün yaklaşık yüzde 16 ila 18'inin azaltılması anlamına geliyor. İşten çıkarmalarda yapay zeka da etkili olacak Imperial Brands, azalan sigara satışları, sıkılaşan düzenlemeler ve artan maliyetler karşısında kârlılığını korumak için yeni bir dönüşüm programı yürütüyor. Şirket, fiyat artışlarının yanı sıra elektronik sigara, nikotin keseleri ve dijitalleşmeye yatırım yapıyor. CEO Lukas Paravicini, işten çıkarmaların yalnızca verimlilik hedefiyle sınırlı olmadığını, şirketi daha fazla veri odaklı ve yeniliklere daha hızlı uyum sağlayan bir yapıya dönüştürmeyi amaçladığını belirtti. Paravicini, bazı iş fonksiyonlarının yapay zeka dahil daha fazla teknolojinin iş süreçlerine entegre edilmesiyle yürütüleceğini ifade etti. Almanya'nın Langenhagen kentindeki tesis ile Tayvan'da daha önce duyurulan fabrika kapanışlarının da yeniden yapılanma sürecine dahil olduğu bildirildi. Rakip tütün devi de 2028'e kadar 9 bin 400 kişiyi çıkaracak Sektörde maliyet azaltma adımları Imperial Brands ile sınırlı değil. Rakip İngiliz tütün şirketi British American Tobacco (BAT), haziran ayında 2028'e kadar yıllık 700 milyon sterlin tasarruf hedeflediğini açıklamıştı. BAT, yaklaşık 47 bin kişilik küresel iş gücünün beşte birine karşılık gelen yaklaşık 9 bin 400 pozisyonu azaltmayı planlıyor. Sigara satışları düşerken alternatif ürünler büyüyor Imperial Brands'in eylül ayında sona eren 2026 mali yılında toplam geliri, özellikle Avrupa'daki sigara satışlarındaki düşüşün etkisiyle yıllık yüzde 1,5 azalarak 31,7 milyar sterline geriledi. articles.titleTr: VakıfBank'tan 742,5 milyon dolarlık finansman hamlesi: Kaynağın adresi belli oldu
articles.summaryTr: VakıfBank, Asya Kalkınma Bankası ve Dünya Bankası kaynaklı toplam 742,5 milyon dolarlık finansman anlaşması imzaladı. Kaynak; deprem bölgesindeki konutlardan KOBİ'lerin yeşil ve dijital dönüşüm yatırımlarına kadar farklı alanlarda kullanılacak.
articles.articleText: VakıfBank'tan 742,5 milyon dolarlık finansman hamlesi: Kaynağın adresi belli oldu - VakıfBank, Asya Kalkınma Bankası ve Dünya Bankası kaynaklı toplam 742,5 milyon dolarlık finansman anlaşması imzaladı. Kaynak; deprem bölgesindeki konutlardan KOBİ'lerin yeşil ve dijital dönüşüm yatırımlarına kadar farklı alanlarda kullanılacak. VakıfBank (VAKBN), Asya Kalkınma Bankası (ADB) ve Dünya Bankası Grubu üyesi Uluslararası İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası (IBRD) kaynaklı iki ayrı finansman anlaşması imzaladığını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yapılan açıklamalara göre banka, ADB ile toplam 500 milyon dolar, IBRD kaynaklarıyla ise 242,5 milyon dolar karşılığı finansman sağlanması için anlaşmaya imza attı. Böylece iki anlaşma kapsamında sağlanan toplam finansman 742,5 milyon dolara ulaştı. ADB kaynaklı 500 milyon doların vadesi 20 yıla kadar uzanıyor VakıfBank'ın Asya Kalkınma Bankası ile imzaladığı 500 milyon dolarlık kredi anlaşması iki ayrı dilimden oluşuyor. Finansmanın 400 milyon dolarlık bölümü T.C. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı garantisi kapsamında ve 20 yıl vadeli olacak. Garanti kapsamında olmayan 100 milyon dolarlık bölümün vadesi ise 5 yıl olarak belirlendi. 400 milyon dolarlık kaynak, depremden etkilenen bölgelerde afete dayanıklı ve enerji verimli konutların inşası, az gelişmiş bölgelerdeki KOBİ'lerin yeşil dönüşüm yatırımları ve kadın girişimciliğinin desteklenmesi için kullanılacak. Kalan 100 milyon dolarlık finansman ise mikro ve küçük ölçekli işletmelerin finansmana erişimini artırmayı hedefliyor. Dünya Bankası kaynaklı 242,5 milyon dolar sanayinin dönüşümüne ayrılacak VakıfBank'ın ikinci anlaşması, Dünya Bankası kaynaklı İkiz Dönüşüm (TransformIndustry) Projesi kapsamında imzalandı. Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanlığı tarafından yürütülen Yeşil Dönüşüm ve Dijital Dönüşüm Programları çerçevesinde sağlanan 242,5 milyon dolarlık finansman, imalat sanayisinde faaliyet gösteren işletmelerin yatırımlarında kullanılacak. Kaynak, ilgili programlar kapsamında teşvik belgesine sahip KOBİ'ler ile orta ve büyük ölçekli işletmelerin yeşil ve dijital dönüşüm yatırımlarına yönlendirilecek. Finansman, T.C. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı aracılığıyla dış borcun ikrazı yöntemiyle sağlanacak. Hedef sürdürülebilir üretim ve rekabet gücünü artırmak Dünya Bankası kaynaklı finansmanla işletmelerin sürdürülebilir üretim kapasitelerinin geliştirilmesi, ileri teknolojilerin üretim süreçlerine entegrasyonunun teşvik edilmesi ve Türk sanayisinin uluslararası rekabet gücünün artırılması hedefleniyor. Böylece VakıfBank'ın iki ayrı uluslararası finansman anlaşması; deprem bölgesinin yeniden inşası, küçük işletmelerin finansmana erişimi ve sanayide yeşil-dijital dönüşüm gibi farklı alanlara kaynak sağlamış olacak.

articles.title: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9327-26 CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today released the agenda for an industry roundtable to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26]. Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. “From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. For the highest quality, select the number nearest your current location. - New York: 646-828-7666 - New Jersey: 551-285-1373 - San Jose: 669-254-5252 or 669-216-1590 - US toll free: 833-568-8864 or 833-435-1820 - US Spanish-language line: 646-964-1167 or 415-449-4000 - International Numbers - Webinar ID: 165 708 9557 - Passcode: 669856 Individuals with additional questions should contact [email protected]. The views, opinions, and information expressed by roundtable participants are solely those of the respective participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission, its staff, or the U.S. government. -CFTC-

news.title: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss
news.summary: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss
news.summaryTr: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
news.articleText: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss - Published Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia, in his first public comments since his shock resignation. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. But he said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia. As the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company. The prospect of Huang returning at this point looks unlikely. The company's board is investigating his conduct, which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive. The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang. Beyond the internal Nvidia investigation, Huang's affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Beijing is set to see the billionaire questioned before multiple committees of US lawmakers in the weeks ahead. The Nvidia founder said he had "made serious mistakes in my personal life". Nonetheless, Huang's statement appeared to show some hope he would be able to move past the major corporate scandal. Huang said people have continued to "reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics". "If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang added. Many technology executives in recent days have praised Huang's role in the artificial intelligence boom. A petition began circulating online over the weekend calling for his reinstatement at the company. Yet, by Monday, many executives were not openly calling for Huang's return. Brad Gerstner, a major tech investor who knows Huang personally and also holds a significant stake in Nvidia, last week wrote an open letter saying that Nvidia could consider Huang's reinstatement. On Monday, Gerstner said during an event hosted by Semafor that his letter had been misunderstood and the investigation into Huang's conduct needed to run its course. While Gerstner questioned the facts around Huang's departure, he added: "I don't know to what degree he misled the board. If I was on a board I would take that very seriously. Let's be clear no one is above the law."

news.title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
news.summary: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
news.summaryTr: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
news.articleText: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements - Published The UK has sanctioned companies it said are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory. The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank. The construction of settlements, which are illegal under international law, has risen sharply in recent years. There has also been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property. Israel is yet to comment on the announcement, but has previously condemned UK sanctions related to West Bank settlements, accusing the Labour government of "systematically acting against the State of Israel". The Palestinian foreign ministry welcomed the sanctions and called on other countries to follow suit. It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the highly sensitive E1 area east of Jerusalem. The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and cut it off from East Jerusalem. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine". The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza. Responding to the announcement, the group said: "Tzav 9 is a movement of abiding citizens from all the political spectrum, and we've always protested peacefully." It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world. The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements and the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK. Miliband said: "Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach. "That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution. "The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable. "We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike." 'New approach' In September, the UK government announced that it would ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements, as well as acting against companies and individuals providing services for settlement expansion. At the time, Miliband said the move marked the beginning of a "new approach" to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which "not only calls out injustice and suffering, but acts". That announcement prompted a furious reaction from Israel, which said it would shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem in retaliation. Last month, most diplomats left the consulate - which handled UK relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem as well as in the West Bank and Gaza - but the UK insisted that the building would not be closing and would operate as a "UK mission". Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them. There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. - Israel opens up bids for highly sensitive West Bank settlement project - Published20 August Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

news.title: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
news.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
news.summaryTr: Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains.
news.articleText: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance Fed Governor Christopher Waller questioned who bears responsibility for fraud, compromised keys and failed transactions as traditional financial assets move onto blockchains. US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller cited the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack while raising questions about security and accountability in tokenized financial markets, suggesting that major institutional transactions may require blockchain systems offering greater privacy and control. Speaking at The Clearing House’s annual conference in New York on Nov. 17, an event bringing together banking and payments industry leaders, Waller questioned who would bear responsibility when fraudsters exploit smart contracts, private keys are compromised, transfers go wrong or assets become stranded on failed blockchains. Waller said the level of security and oversight required could depend on the importance of the financial transactions involved: For example, systemically important financial transactions may call for the most conservative designs. These designs might trade some of the developer creativity found on purely permissionless, open networks in favor of greater privacy and control. The expansion of tokenized finance would also require clear legal frameworks governing ownership rights, custody and settlement, he said, arguing that governance and legal protections are as important as technical safeguards in building trust. Waller’s remarks came as four Democratic senators pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over safeguards for tokenized stocks. In a letter released Monday, the lawmakers questioned who would be responsible for shares transferred outside regulated platforms and whether regulators could freeze or recover the tokens. Related: Custodia Bank loses Supreme Court bid for direct Fed payment access Barr warns of AI-related cybersecurity risks Waller wasn’t the only Federal Reserve governor to raise concerns about emerging financial technologies this week. His remarks followed a Monday speech by fellow Fed Governor Michael Barr, who warned that artificial intelligence could introduce new cybersecurity risks as financial institutions increasingly adopt the technology. Barr said AI-enabled attackers were exploiting vulnerabilities previously considered too difficult to target, while autonomous AI systems could behave in ways that undermine security controls “Attackers only need to be right once, while defenders need to be right all the time,” Barr said. He also said major banks had reported finding AI agents attempting to take actions in retail customer accounts without being able to verify their authenticity or authorization, highlighting the need for stronger authentication and security controls. news.title: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
news.summary: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".

news.titleTr: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
news.summaryTr: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".
news.articleText: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington - Published President Donald Trump has said the US is taking "very seriously" the potential for any Iranian plot to attack Washington DC, after he was asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments. In the Philippines, where he attended the Asean Summit, Trump nodded when asked by a journalist about the report that Tehran was planning to detonate a so-called dirty bomb in the US capital and said: "We're looking into it." CNN cited unnamed US intelligence officials suggesting Iran could target senior figures in Trump's administration with such an attack. Iran called the claim "baseless." Concerns about dirty bombs grew after the 9/11 attacks in 2001, although no such attack has ever occurred. Such a device would contain radioactive material - such as uranium - which would be scattered through the air when its conventional explosive detonated. The BBC has not independently verified CNN's reporting. During his comments to reporters in Manila, Trump was asked whether there was reason to believe an attack was imminent. "I hope it's not," he said, "but we take it very seriously because they [the Iranians] happen to be crazy." In a statement before Trump's comments, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis wrote: "We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland." Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rebutted the CNN article and other US reports. He posted on X: "Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations." Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's parliamentary speaker and chief negotiator in indirect talks with the US, responded to the report saying it was part of a "messaging operation". "Same false flags, same war mongering, new logos," he wrote on X. Mick Mulroy, a former CIA paramilitary officer and deputy assistant defence secretary, told the BBC: "A dirty bomb is not difficult to make or deploy." "Although it is not a weapon of mass destruction, it can be a weapon of mass disruption," he added. Imran Bayoumi, a geostrategy expert with the Atlantic Council in Washington DC and former policy adviser to the defence department, said that it remains "unclear how serious" would be the threat of a supposed Iranian dirty bomb. "But Iran has planned and threatened to attack the US in the past," he said. "It is also unclear why this report is becoming public now." It comes as intelligence officials and members of the Trump administration seek congressional renewal of a key national security law. Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (Fisa), which allows the US to spy on foreign nationals, expires next March.

news.title: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
news.summary: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
news.summaryTr: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
news.articleText: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge - Published The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions. Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted. Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around. At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide. The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours. Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet. Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles. Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions. "It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection. But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful. "It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that." From the damage, it looks like Russia targeted the same spot on the bridge with a volley of three missiles, aiming to keep the road closed for as long as possible. A major recovery operation is under way, with firefighters and engineers in fluorescent overalls working to evaluate the extent of the damage. But it looks like the disruption will continue for some time. Further along the Dnipro River, the Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was also hit on Monday night, with four missiles. The metro line across it was suspended for a while, although by mid-afternoon it had been restored. The mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said road transport in one direction was also being partially restored. On the Pivnichnyi bridge, a man with a bag of tennis rackets on his back was gazing at the crater in front of him. He was heading home from the courts after he had travelled on foot to the left bank. "It is upsetting," Anatolii told us. "Then when you read the news of what our side did to the Crimea bridge, you do feel a bit better." That is because there was a battle of the bridges overnight. Ukrainian missiles hit the one Russia had built to occupied Crimea, and caused serious damage. That bridge is prized by Russian President Vladimir Putin personally, a symbol of his illegal 2014 takeover. Ukrainians loathe it for the same reason and now a section has collapsed into the sea, along with its towering arch. To many here, the timing feels significant: a blow to Putin's image, just as he wants to seem most powerful at this week's summit with the US and China. But for Kyiv resident Antonina, today is just another challenge to overcome. The 67-year-old, who we met pulling a shopping trolley through the debris on a bridge in the Ukrainian capital, was heading to see her son on the right bank, but taxi drivers were charging a fortune to go round, so she decided to walk. "What else could I do?" she shrugged. "It was a very scary night. It felt like something exploded right over my head. We will get through this, but I just wish the war would end." - Published52 minutes ago

news.titleTr: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
news.summaryTr: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
news.articleText: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers - Published After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections. The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness. PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year. "These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination." He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission. Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates. US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years. Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections. Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status". "Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans. "Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities." The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards". The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths. But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems. The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns. An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials. Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database. Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics. The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge. President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine. Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates. "It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top." news.summaryTr: Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, fon soruşturmalarında 75 kişiden yaklaşık 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildiğini açıkladı. Soruşturma kapsamında 129 şüpheli tutuklu, 289 şüpheli ise adli kontrol altında bulunuyor.
news.articleText: Adalet Bakanı Gürlek açıkladı: Fon soruşturmasında 40,4 milyar TL geri alındı - Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, fon soruşturmalarında 75 kişiden yaklaşık 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildiğini açıkladı. Soruşturma kapsamında 129 şüpheli tutuklu, 289 şüpheli ise adli kontrol altında bulunuyor. Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturmalarında gelinen son durumu açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturmaların yeni deliller doğrultusunda genişletildiğini belirten Gürlek, bugüne kadar 498 şüphelinin soruşturma kapsamına alındığını bildirdi. Gürlek'in paylaştığı bilgilere göre 129 şüpheli tutuklu, 289 şüpheli hakkında ise adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanıyor. Hakkında yakalama kararı bulunan 54 şüpheliye yönelik çalışmalar sürerken, gözaltındaki 22 şüphelinin adli işlemleri devam ediyor. 75 kişiden 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildi Soruşturmalar kapsamında gönüllü iade ve geri kazanım çalışmaları sonucunda 75 kişiden yaklaşık 40,4 milyar TL tahsil edildi. Gürlek, gönüllü iadenin hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmayacağını vurgulayarak, “Gönüllü iade yapılması, tek başına hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmaz” ifadelerini kullandı. 417 kişi ve 149 şirketin malvarlığına tedbir Suçtan elde edildiği değerlendirilen gelirlerin kaçırılmasını önlemek amacıyla 417 gerçek kişi ve 149 tüzel kişinin malvarlıkları hakkında el koyma ve dondurma kararı uygulandığını açıklayan Gürlek, para hareketleri, malvarlığı devirleri ve bağlantılı hesapların ayrıntılı incelendiğini belirtti. Denetim süreçlerine ilişkin iddialar da inceleniyor Gürlek, fon yöneticileri ve piyasa aktörlerinin yanı sıra denetim süreçlerine ilişkin iddiaların da soruşturma kapsamında değerlendirildiğini bildirdi. Kamu görevlileri dahil hukuki sorumluluk doğurabilecek tüm hususların yetkili adli makamlarca incelendiğini belirten Gürlek, hiçbir iddianın peşinen doğru kabul edilmeyeceğini ve somut delillerin göz ardı edilmeyeceğini ifade etti. Fon Koordinasyon Kurulu'nun 10'uncu toplantısı yapıldı Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz başkanlığında, ilgili kurumların temsilcilerinin katılımıyla 10'uncu Fon Koordinasyon Kurulu Toplantısı gerçekleştirildi. Toplantıda soruşturmaların seyri, mali incelemeler, uygulanan tedbirler ve yatırımcıların haklarının korunmasına yönelik çalışmalar değerlendirildi.
